input.quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman. If Sparkling terminates this Agreement pursuant to this Section 17(b), Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
input.rationale: Compliant at the fallback. Section 17(b) (p0118) gives us, the Customer, an unconditional at-will termination right — "at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice" — with no cause, trigger, consent or condition attached, and the full clause is quoted above so the whole of the exit mechanic is visible: the only consequences are ceasing use at the end of the notice period and certifying return/destruction of Software, Documentation and Codes. No early-termination fee, penalty, liquidated damages or non-refundability charge appears here or in the fee provisions. Garman, the Vendor, has no convenience right at all: its only triggers are the insolvency events and uncured material default in Section 17(c) (p0128), and Section 10 maintenance simply runs as a renewable one-year term, so the walk-away scenario (Vendor convenience termination on short notice) is not engaged. The clause therefore satisfies every material fallback term — Customer notice within the 60–90 day window, no early-termination fee above three months' fees, no Vendor convenience right. Two points fall short of preferred and are noted rather than redlined, per the playbook's classification semantics: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and the Agreement is silent on a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on a 17(b) exit (refund of fees for services not yet rendered arises only on termination for Garman's default under 17(c)). Given the penalty-free exit and the perpetual, fee-contingent licence in Section 17(a) rather than a multi-year committed term, a redline would be disproportionate and none is proposed. For the record, the deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" check is a keyword false negative: the clause grants the right without using the words "for convenience"; we would raise the wording only as an optional clarification in negotiation, not as a redline.
